name: noir-strings-spoken-sermon
style: mid-90s New York crime-saga hip hop, slow cinematic noir: a mournful minor-key violin phrase looping like an old detective-film score, bowed cello droning underneath, sparse dusty kick and a heavy dry snare at 82 BPM for a slow head nod, lots of air around the voice. Lead is a huge, slow, cavernous bass baritone, Brooklyn vowels, delivering each rule like a minister reading scripture, mostly talked rather than rapped, deliberate rests between lines, a dry smirk under the gravity. Each counted number lands in a big stone-church echo; the rest stays bone-dry and intimate. Chilly, patient, final.
exclude: autotune, trap hi-hats, 808 bass slides, melodic hook, gospel choir, female voice, rapid double-time flow, EDM, pop, horn fanfare, bright major chords, vinyl crackle overload
lyrics:
[Intro: violin loop alone, a pulpit murmur, unhurried]
Uh. Uh-huh.
Money printer manual. Page one. Take notes.

[Sermon: talked like scripture, a held breath after every number]
[Numbers ring in the stone church]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Numbers ring in the stone church]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Numbers ring in the stone church]
Number six: no credit? Nah, they live on the slate,
and you're paying it back in the price on your plate.

[Numbers ring in the stone church]
Number seven: keep the family out the business,
Treasury and the bank in one bed, God as my witness.

[Numbers ring in the stone church]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Benediction: beat cuts, just cello, a near-whisper verdict]
And the fix, from the future? Easy.
No hand on the printer.
[End]
